slides.headline: AN AI CHARGED SOMEONE $8.5 BILLION
slides.subline: IT WAS GOING TO THE RED CROSS

slides.headline: A CIRCLE K CHECKOUT SNAPPED
slides.body: A Reddit user says a Circle K self-checkout AI tried to process a charge worth billions that nobody asked for. The post hit nearly 20,000 upvotes in under 9 hours

slides.headline: IT PICKED THE RED CROSS
slides.body: The post says the AI decided the customer owed $8.5 billion to the Red Cross. The machine picked the charity, picked the amount, and created the entire donation in one made-up transaction

slides.headline: CHECKOUT NEVER NEEDED AI
slides.body: Thousands of comments asked: why put AI in a checkout? It scans items, adds prices, and takes your card. That's it. Zero thinking required

slides.headline: AI BROKE WHAT ALREADY WORKED
slides.body: The businesses winning with AI aren't putting it at checkout. They put it where humans waste hours every week on emails, scheduling, and reports. That's where AI turns from a headline embarrassment to a real edge

slides.headline: THIS MACHINE IS STILL RUNNING
slides.body: Companies are shoving AI into everything that already works. Follow @yaffeai, you'll want to see who's next. Send this to anyone who uses self-checkout

caption:
Swipe to see what happened when a self-checkout AI decided to think for itself 🤖

A Reddit user says a Circle K self-checkout machine with AI tried to process a payment of over $8.5 billion to the Red Cross, a transaction the customer never requested, and the post blew up to nearly 20,000 upvotes in 9 hours with thousands asking why AI is being shoved into a process that already works.

Companies are racing to add AI to everything, but the ones making real money put it where humans waste hours, not where a scanner already does the job.
